scope.title: Central Europe and German/Italian source families
scope.sourceStrategy: Regional/state archives and constitutional collections; establish small-state and imperial scope before statistics.
scope.priorityRationale: Early source-family batches prioritise long snapshot presence, broad period potential and national archival/constitutional collections. Source availability is a planning expectation, not an entity-by-entity research finding. Families remain indivisible; no periods are researched now.

difficultCases.question: Separate source naming variation, constituent governments and potential unification/succession; no overlap-derived chain.

limitations: All accepted dossiers are partial. Curated bounds are not complete state lifetimes. Missing currency, statistics, flags, offices, seats and predecessor/successor links remain omitted rather than inferred.

The unified Two Sicilies kingdom dates from 1816. The assigned 1800/1815 raw label is not accepted at either snapshot; sourced 1817–1819 between-snapshot coverage does not count as snapshot political coverage.
Anhalt is not resolved to one of the separate Bernburg, Dessau or Köthen states. The source referent requires geometry/source-family review.
Hohenzollern is not resolved arbitrarily to Hechingen or Sigmaringen. Independent archives distinguish the principalities.
Italy 1922–1929 and July 1943–May 1945 remain gaps; competing wartime administrations are not collapsed into a single royal government. June 1946 royal transfer retains month precision.
Czechoslovakia 1918–1920, 1938–October 1945 and 1946–1948 remain gaps; constitutional adoption is not substituted for unverified commencement in 1920.
Lucca 1815 was administered provisionally by Austria; Maria Luisa’s actual government begins in 1817 at source year precision.
Restored Italian duchies are not projected into 1800. Lombardy and Venetia are administrative governments, not sovereign states.
Baden and Hanover retain especially narrow 1815 institutional coverage. No population/GDP/flag enrichment was attempted.

validation.fullPeriodicRegression: Next scheduled at Batch 05; shared production architecture and resolver unchanged.
limitations: Expected missing local boundary files use existing upstream fallback; favicon 404 ignored.
Three initial generated-output tests were stale before regeneration; a missing review interval was completed with sourced review bounds.
An existing coverage reconciliation test exposed an audit-only planning count defect for between-snapshot dossiers. Fixed to count snapshot resolver availability; all tests pass.

sources.title: 17 marzo 1861: Unità nazionale
sources.institution: Italian Ministry of Culture / State Archives of Modena
sources.usage: Law of 17 March 1861; Vittorio Emanuele II became King of Italy; parliamentary documents.

sources.title: Statuto Albertino, 1848
sources.usage: Representative hereditary monarchy; royal executive; King, Senate and Deputies as legislative institutions. Original Sardinian constitutional text, not a claim of democratic suffrage.

sources.title: 150° anniversario dell’Unità d’Italia, 2011
sources.usage: Historical account of the liberal monarchical state and completion of unification.

sources.title: Benito Mussolini
sources.usage: Head of government 31 October 1922–25 July 1943; dictatorship consolidated by 1925–29 legislation.

sources.title: 2 giugno 1946 — 2 giugno 2016
sources.usage: Postwar coalition government; 9 May 1946 royal abdication; referendum versus official proclamation of the republic on 18 June.

sources.title: Costituzione della Repubblica Italiana
sources.usage: Signed 27 December 1947; force 1 January 1948; republican constitutional settlement and presidential seat.

sources.title: Il potere di grazia — Presidenti della Repubblica
sources.usage: Archival term-start dates for Einaudi, Gronchi and Segni. Modern statistics are not used as historical dossier data.

sources.title: Vittorio Emanuele I
sources.usage: Royal exile in Cagliari, return to Turin in May 1814, restoration and abdication on 13 March 1821.

sources.title: Sicilie, Regno delle Due
sources.usage: Unified kingdom founded in 1816; Ferdinand I; prevents retroactive mapping in 1800/1815.

sources.title: Regno lombardo veneto (1815–1866)
sources.institution: Italian Ministry of Culture — SAN archival inventory
sources.usage: 7 April 1815 patent; two separate governments with governors, councils and seats at Milan and Venice. Later erroneous 14 March 1861 date in this inventory is not used.

sources.title: Governi di Lucca — archival institutional history
sources.usage: Austrian provisional administration 1814–1817; Werklein in 1815; actual ducal administration from 1817, not 1815.

sources.title: L’Archivio di Stato di Modena
sources.institution: State Archives of Modena — Archivi italiani series
sources.usage: Pages 22–23: restored Austro-Este government, Francesco IV, centralised ducal reform plan of 28 August 1814.

sources.title: Storia dell’Archivio di Stato di Parma
sources.usage: Bourbon, French and Maria Luigia periods; 1814 grant; arrival and archival decree in 1816; Parma as pre-unification capital.

sources.title: Ducato di Parma, Piacenza e Guastalla — 20 lire, 1815
sources.institution: Istituto Poligrafico e Zecca dello Stato — Museo della Zecca
sources.usage: Primary dated coin and catalogued issuing authority Maria Luigia; duchess title. Mint location is not a capital claim.

sources.title: Il Granducato di Toscana e Roma — archivio diplomatico
sources.institution: Italian Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Historical Diplomatic Archive
sources.usage: Introduction: Ferdinand III restored 20 April 1814; Secretariat of State and restored Florentine administration; dated 1814/1815 documents.

sources.title: Carta corografica dello Stato Pontificio, 1817
sources.institution: Italian Ministry of Culture / State Archives
sources.usage: Restoration in 1814; Pius VII and Consalvi reforms in 1816; 1817 provincial edict.

sources.title: History of Parliament
sources.institution: Chamber of Deputies, Parliament of the Czech Republic
sources.usage: 1920 constitutional adoption; 28 October 1945 provisional assembly; 1948 Communist constitutional order; 11 July 1960 constitution. Erroneous 1946 election interval in leaflet is not used.

sources.title: Ústava Československé socialistické republiky, 1960
sources.institution: Chamber of Deputies — original constitutional text
sources.usage: Article 4 Communist Party role; article 109 Prague capital; article 112 commencement on adoption.

sources.title: Königswürde (1806), Ferdinand Kramer
sources.institution: Historisches Lexikon Bayerns — Bavarian State Library scholarly project
sources.usage: 1 January 1806 proclamation, earlier electoral title, Maximilian Joseph’s offices and Munich residence.

sources.title: Umbruch und Aufbruch — Das Archivwesen nach 1800
sources.usage: Baden chapter, especially printed pages 303–307: grand-ducal administration, ministries, 1815 state handbook. Narrow institutional coverage, not reconstructed full constitutional history.

sources.title: Bremens Selbständigkeit
sources.usage: Imperial city, sovereignty in 1806, French annexation 1810, restoration of old civic constitution 1813 and German Confederation 1815.

sources.title: Restauration, Revolution, Reform — Birgit Steinke
sources.institution: Hamburg Geschichtsbuch — publicly supported historical education
sources.usage: 8 June 1815 Confederation charter; restored civic institutions; Free and Hanseatic formal style from 1819.

sources.title: Hannovers Geschichte in Zahlen
sources.usage: 1814 elevation to kingdom; residence and personal union context.

sources.title: Residenzstadt Braunschweig
sources.usage: Ducal residence; restoration after French domination; Friedrich Wilhelm died 16 June 1815.

sources.title: Geschichte des Oberlandesgerichts
sources.institution: Higher Regional Court of Braunschweig / Lower Saxony Justice
sources.usage: 14 January 1814 restored ducal judicial constitution and court hierarchy.

sources.title: Holsten — Finn Mygind
sources.institution: Den Store Danske / Lex scholarly reference
sources.usage: Danish dynastic rule, end of imperial status in 1806; Frederik VI as Duke of Holstein in German Confederation from 1815.

sources.title: Hohenzollern — historical presentation
sources.usage: Distinct Hechingen and Sigmaringen principalities; no single-state mapping justified for aggregate raw label.

sources.title: Landes- und archivkundliches Vademecum Sachsen-Anhalt
sources.usage: Separate Bernburg, Dessau and Köthen states after 1793; unification only in 1863.
